hero.headline: Treasure Coast Traffic Report: Major Ramp and Road Closures Planned July 12-17
hero.teaser:
Motorists should prepare for overnight interstate ramp closures, extended neighborhood road closures and lane restrictions across Martin, St. Lucie and Indian River counties.

Driv
hero.body:
Motorists should prepare for overnight interstate ramp closures, extended neighborhood road closures and lane restrictions across Martin, St. Lucie and Indian River counties.

Drivers across the Treasure Coast could encounter delays during the week of July 10-17 as construction and maintenance continue on several major roadways.

The Florida Department of Transportation's latest weekly traffic report identifies multiple lane restrictions across Martin, St. Lucie and Indian River counties. FDOT placed additional emphasis on full road, ramp and bridge closures expected to have the greatest effect on motorists.

## Major closures to know about

### I-95 exit to Bridge Road closing overnight in Martin County

The southbound Interstate 95 exit ramp to County Road 708, also known as Bridge Road, at Exit 96 will be closed from **8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Sunday, July 12, through Thursday, July 16.**

Drivers will be directed to exit at Kanner Highway, travel south on Pratt Whitney Road and then head east on Bridge Road.

The closure is needed for roadway construction. Weather-related contingency dates are scheduled for July 19-23.

### Port St. Lucie neighborhood roads could close for several days

Extended closures are planned along several side streets near the SW Port St. Lucie Boulevard widening project.

Closures may begin at **7 a.m. Monday, July 13, and continue until 5 p.m. Friday, July 17,** on portions of SW Jaslo Avenue, SW Jacoby Avenue, SW McCullough Avenue, SW McCall Road and SW McHord Avenue.

The roads will close intermittently for drainage and utility installation. FDOT said adjacent roads will not be closed at the same time, and access to homes and businesses will be maintained.

Detours will generally use SW Paar Drive, SW McCain Street, SW McIntyre Street, SW Kabane Street and other nearby roads, depending on the closure location.

### I-95 ramp to Orange Avenue closing in Fort Pierce

The northbound I-95 exit ramp to westbound State Road 68, or Orange Avenue, will be closed from **8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Sunday, July 12, through Thursday, July 16.**

Motorists will be detoured using the exit to eastbound Orange Avenue, northbound Jenkins Road and westbound Loop Road before returning to westbound Orange Avenue.

The work includes paving and lighting installation. Contingency dates are July 19-23.

## Martin County traffic impacts

Motorists should expect overnight lane closures on I-95 between Bridge Road and the Martin-St. Lucie county line. Up to two lanes may close in each direction during overnight hours for milling, resurfacing and signage work.

On U.S. 1 in Stuart, two lanes may close intermittently between Fischer Street and Decker Avenue from 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Sunday through Friday for sign installation.

A1A between Shore Village Terrace and the Jensen Beach Causeway may be reduced to one lane at times from Monday through Friday for drainage work and pavement widening. Flaggers will maintain two-way traffic through the work zone.

Martin Highway between Stuart West Boulevard and Citrus Boulevard may also have intermittent overnight lane closures Tuesday through Thursday.

FDOT is additionally warning drivers in advance about several upcoming I-95 ramp closures at Martin Highway and Kanner Highway later in July and early August.

## St. Lucie County traffic impacts

Port St. Lucie Boulevard between Seafury Lane and Lennard Road may have daytime lane closures Monday through Friday. Two lanes may close overnight from Sunday through Friday for drainage work, milling and repaving.

U.S. 1 between Jennings Road and Golden Oak Trail may also have lane restrictions during both daytime and overnight hours.

On SW Port St. Lucie Boulevard, one lane may close between Jordin Avenue and Alcantarra Boulevard from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. Monday through Friday as crews continue the widening project.

Up to two lanes may close overnight on I-95 between Glades Cut-Off Road and the area just south of Okeechobee Road for milling and repaving.

Midway Road between Florida's Turnpike and Selvitz Road may continue to have intermittent weekday lane closures through September as part of the roadway widening project.

## North Causeway marine restrictions

The new A1A North Causeway Bridge remains open to vehicle traffic, but significant restrictions are planned for boaters using the Intracoastal Waterway.

The existing drawbridge will not open to marine traffic from 7 a.m. Thursday, July 16, through 6 p.m. Saturday, July 18. Boats capable of passing beneath the bridge without an opening may continue through.

Additional single-leaf openings, partial channel obstructions and temporary full channel closures are scheduled through July 24 as crews remove portions of the former drawbridge.

FDOT said the marine work will not affect vehicle traffic on the new bridge.

## Indian River County traffic impacts

One lane may remain closed on the 17th Street bridges between Indian River Boulevard and Indian Bay Drive as bridge rehabilitation continues.

At the new I-95 interchange at Oslo Road, one or two interstate lanes may close overnight Sunday through Thursday for bridge work, milling and resurfacing.

On 90th Avenue between Sebastian Boulevard and 87th Street, one lane may close overnight Sunday through Friday for construction associated with the 85th Street widening project.

Drivers traveling near Sebastian Inlet should also expect intermittent lane or shoulder closures on A1A through Friday, July 17. Flaggers will direct motorists through the work zone.

Sections of the north and south parking lots at Sebastian Inlet State Park will remain closed during construction of the new bridge. The closures are expected to continue through spring 2032, although the park and portions of both parking lots remain open.

## Plan ahead

Construction schedules may change because of weather or other unforeseen conditions. Motorists should allow additional travel time, follow posted detours and use caution around workers and equipment.

Real-time interstate traffic conditions are available through Florida 511. Updated lane closure information is also available through FDOT District Four.

cards.headline: FDLE conducts 24 immigration arrests in Martin County as enforcement methods shift
cards.body:
The Florida Department of Law Enforcement conducted 24 immigration arrests in Martin County on Tuesday, according to data kept by FDLE and confirmed by the Martin County Sheriff's Office. The arrests come as immigration attorneys across South Florida report a shift in how federal and local law enforcement are carrying out immigration detentions, with fewer high-profile operations that spark public outrage and raise legal concerns.

Renata Castro, an immigration attorney based in Coral Springs, said her firm has seen more detained cases in recent months. Castro said many of the current detentions result from traffic-related stops that lead to immigration arrests. She noted the change appears to coincide with Markwayne Mullin replacing Kristi Noem as Homeland Security Secretary in March.

Castro said the approach under Noem was markedly different from what attorneys are seeing now. "What we saw during Kristi Noem's term was a lot of arrests without a warrant, just a big spectacle overall," Castro said. Immigration attorneys previously questioned the legality of many detentions carried out during Noem's tenure. Castro said she does not have those same legal concerns about the current approach. "These are arrests without warrants, but still following the safeguards that the law, particularly local law enforcement, has to abide by, and that's why we're seeing an uptick in detention numbers," Castro said.

According to NBC News, ICE arrested 10,000 people over five days this month. WPTV reached out to ICE and FDLE for comment.

cards.headline: DEA seizes 120 pounds of meth in Palm Beach County, warns surge spreading to Treasure Coast
cards.teaser: Federal agents seized about 54 kilos of methamphetamine, nearly 120 pounds, in Palm Beach County in just two days. DEA agents warn the surge is beginning to spread to the Treasure Coast.
cards.body:
Federal agents in Palm Beach County are sounding the alarm over what they call an unprecedented surge in methamphetamine, one they say is being fueled by the rising cost of cocaine. Inside the DEA's West Palm Beach office, federal agents packed up 12 kilos, about 26 pounds, of pure crystal meth, part of a larger haul of about 54 kilos, nearly 120 pounds, pulled off Palm Beach County streets in just two days. One seizure was laced with deadly fentanyl. Special Agent Kevin Bobbitt said the scale of what agents are seeing is unlike anything he has encountered in South Florida.

Bobbitt said the surge is tied directly to economics. As cocaine prices are high, with an ounce now selling for $600 to $1,000, more users are turning to meth as a cheaper alternative. An ounce of meth can cost less than half that, ranging from $280 to $500. Bobbitt said from a pure economic standpoint, it is much cheaper to get your hands on methamphetamine. The problem is not limited to trafficking. Bobbitt said a meth lab was recently busted in Palm Beach County, and the surge is beginning to spread beyond the county's borders.

Bobbitt said the problem is spreading to counties in the Treasure Coast as well. While those areas are not seeing the same volume yet, he said he is sure it is coming. According to a 2026 White House report, in some states overdose deaths involving meth have surpassed those from fentanyl. Bobbitt said agents are working aggressively to dismantle the organizations behind the surge. He said they are attacking these organizations everywhere they can, with the idea being to drive them out of the location and make it unattractive as a distribution point.

Jim and Adrienne Tichy run a halfway house called The Lodge at Delray Beach. They have not only witnessed the surge in meth firsthand, but also its devastating consequences. Jim Tichy said it is a whole new animal with the methamphetamines. Adrienne Tichy said people are coming in younger and younger and it is terrible, with each family having a different sorrow story. While federal agents work to disrupt the supply, the Tichys are focused on the other side of the crisis, targeting demand through treatment. Adrienne Tichy said their end of it comes after treatment and detox to work with the life skills, the information, and the knowledge, then gradually letting them go into the world, hopefully with success.

cards.headline: South Florida immigration attorneys report shift in federal enforcement tactics under new Homeland Security leadership
cards.body:
South Florida immigration attorneys are observing a change in how federal and local law enforcement conduct immigration arrests, with fewer high-profile raids and a shift toward traffic-related detentions. The change appears to coincide with Markwayne Mullin replacing Kristi Noem as Homeland Security Secretary in March.

Renata Castro, an immigration attorney based in Coral Springs, said she has seen more detained cases and traffic-related detentions resulting in immigration detention. Castro said the approach under Noem was markedly different. "What we saw during Kristi Noem's term was a lot of arrests without a warrant, just a big spectacle overall," Castro said. Immigration attorneys previously questioned the legality of many detentions carried out during Noem's tenure. Castro said she does not have the same legal questions about the current approach. "These are arrests without warrants, but still following the safeguards that the law, particularly local law enforcement, has to abide by, and that's why we're seeing an uptick in detention numbers," Castro said.

According to NBC News, ICE arrested 10,000 people over five days this month. According to data kept by the Florida Department of Law Enforcement, 24 immigration arrests were conducted in Martin County on Tuesday. The Martin County Sheriff's Office confirms FDLE was the agency behind those arrests.

The shift in enforcement tactics represents a change in how immigration enforcement operates in the region. Castro said the current arrests, while still conducted without warrants, follow the safeguards that local law enforcement must abide by, which she attributes to the uptick in detention numbers. The increased numbers of detentions combined with the changed methodology mark a new phase in immigration enforcement across South Florida, moving away from what Castro characterized as the spectacle approach of the previous administration.

cards.headline: New Aldi opens in Hobe Sound as grocery prices rise 2.8% this year
cards.teaser: A new Aldi store opened Thursday at 8867 Southeast Bridge Road in Hobe Sound, offering Martin County shoppers lower-priced groceries as food costs continue to c.
cards.body:
A new Aldi store opened Thursday at 8867 Southeast Bridge Road in Hobe Sound, bringing more affordable grocery options to Martin County shoppers. Customers Cheryl and Tony Cooperman said they are excited to have an affordable option close to their home. Cheryl Cooperman said grocery prices are getting expensive and are changing the way she shops. She said they are the type of people who never used to look at prices, but now she will go with what is on sale instead of just what they want, something they never used to do.

The store opening comes as the USDA expects grocery prices to rise 2.8% this year. Fruits and vegetables are seeing an increase of less than 1%. Egg prices are dropping, and beef prices fell 1.3% from April to May, though wholesale beef prices remain at all-time highs for this time of year. Pork rose 1% from April to May, and chicken prices rose 1.3% over the same period. Shoppers James and Harry said Thursday they do not expect relief at the register anytime soon, saying prices are going to stay inflated and are not going to go down. They said stores like Aldi, which often have lower prices than other stores, can make a difference for everyday shoppers because there is nobody who is not feeling the price increase.

cards.headline: Florida back-to-school sales tax holiday runs July 20 through August 20
cards.teaser: Florida families can save on school supplies, clothing, computers and learning aids during the state's 32-day tax-free shopping period.
cards.body:
Florida's annual back-to-school sales tax holiday runs from July 20 through Aug. 20, 2026, providing 32 days of tax-free shopping on qualifying purchases. The holiday covers clothing, bags and accessories under $100 per item, school supplies under $50 per item, learning aids and puzzles under $30 per item, and computers and accessories under $1,500 per item. Qualifying clothing includes shirts, pants, dresses, shoes, uniforms and athletic wear, while bags include backpacks, handbags, diaper bags and fanny packs. Excluded items include briefcases, suitcases, watches, jewelry, skis, swim fins and roller blades. Tax-free school supplies include pens, pencils, notebooks, binders, scissors, glue, lunch boxes, flashcards, jigsaw puzzles and educational toys. Qualifying computers include laptops, desktops, tablets, electronic book readers and calculators, along with accessories such as keyboards, mice, monitors without TV tuners, printers, modems, routers and educational software.

Items ordered online during the holiday period qualify for the exemption even if delivered after Aug. 20. Items purchased with rain checks issued during the holiday remain tax-free, and using gift cards to buy eligible items qualifies regardless of when the gift card was purchased. The tax exemption is not available at theme parks, entertainment complexes, hotels, public lodging establishments or airports. Florida retailers have no option to opt out of the sales tax holiday, and all qualifying purchases must be processed tax-free during the designated period.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie teen named Southeast Youth of the Year surprised with World Cup trip
cards.teaser: Enrique Rosario Liz, a Port St. Lucie teenager and Southeast Region Youth of the Year for Boys & Girls Clubs of America, will serve as a flag bearer at the FIFA World Cup finals.
cards.body:
Enrique Rosario Liz was surprised at the Boys & Girls Club of St. Lucie County in Fort Pierce with news that he will serve as one of 12 club members from across the country selected to be an official Coca-Cola flag bearer at the FIFA World Cup finals on July 19. The Port St. Lucie teenager had been named Youth of the Year for the Southeast Region of the Boys & Girls Clubs of America and had no idea the World Cup trip was coming. The surprise came through the Boys & Girls Clubs of America partnership with the Coca-Cola Company.

Rosario Liz had been preparing for move-in at the University of Florida and an internship but said the World Cup had been on his mind. He said his time was being taken up by the World Cup, forcing his parents to watch every game. When the box containing the news was walked into the room surrounded by fellow club members, Rosario Liz said it was crazy and insane. He received official gear inside the box along with the trip. Rosario Liz said the club helped him find what his leadership style was going to be and redefined his definition of leadership. He told younger club members to stay with their Boys & Girls Clubs because he wants to see each and every one of them in the same position he is in now.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie ranked 67th most stressed city in US, 42nd most financially stressed
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie ranked as the 67th most stressed city in the United States and 42nd most financially stressed, according to a new WalletHub study that compared 182 cities across 39 metrics.
cards.body:
A new study released this month by WalletHub examined stress levels across 182 cities in the United States. The study compared cities across 39 metrics, which included average weekly work hours, unemployment rate, divorce and suicide rates. Port St. Lucie was tabbed as the 67th most stressed city in the U.S., with the report citing that the city is the 42nd most financially stressed in America.

Jacksonville is the most stressed city in Florida, ranking 37th in the U.S. In South Florida, Miami was on the list at number 50, with affordable housing being fourth worst in the U.S., and Fort Lauderdale at number 83. WalletHub analyst Chip Lupo said cities with high crime rates, weak economies, less effective public health and congested transportation systems naturally lead to elevated stress levels for residents. The report found that money, health and the economy all remain top stressors. Topping the list of most stressed cities in the U.S. were Detroit, Baltimore, Cleveland, Memphis and Shreveport, Louisiana. Fremont, California, in the Bay Area, topped the list of least stressed cities, followed by South Burlington, Vermont, and Bismarck and Fargo, North Dakota.

cards.headline: Jupiter Inlet Lighthouse offers 165 years of history with 105-step climb to panoramic views
cards.teaser: The Jupiter Inlet Lighthouse, built in 1860, has guided ships along Florida's Atlantic coast for more than 165 years. The 105-step climb to the top offers panoramic views of the Atlantic Ocean and the Jupiter Inlet.
cards.body:
The Jupiter Inlet Lighthouse features a striking red brick tower rising high above the inlet. Built in 1860, the lighthouse has guided countless ships along Florida's Atlantic coast for more than 165 years. The 105-step climb to the top takes visitors up a narrow spiral staircase that lighthouse keepers once climbed night after night to keep the powerful Fresnel lens shining for mariners.

From the gallery at the top, panoramic views show the Atlantic Ocean stretching to the east, while the turquoise waters of the Jupiter Inlet meet the Loxahatchee and Indian rivers below. Boats glide through the channel in the waters below. The museum grounds include restored historic buildings where visitors can learn about the lighthouse's past, from its construction before the Civil War to its years as an active Coast Guard station.

hero.headline: Justin Bieber, Madonna, Shakira join World Cup final halftime show
hero.teaser: Justin Bieber will join headliners Madonna, Shakira and BTS for the World Cup's star-studded halftime show at the final outside New York on July 19.
hero.body:
Justin Bieber will bring his swag to the World Cup's star-studded, Super Bowl-style halftime show, joining fellow headliners Madonna, Shakira and BTS, FIFA announced Wednesday. Afrobeats star Burna Boy, Venezuelan conductor Gustavo Dudamel and the PS22 Chorus, a choir of elementary school students based in Staten Island, New York, will also perform, the last joined by Coldplay. The 11-minute halftime performance, curated by Coldplay's Chris Martin, will take place during the final outside New York on July 19. The show will support the FIFA Global Citizen Education Fund, which is raising $100 million to help children access education and soccer.

Of all the performances, the addition of Burna Boy is particularly noteworthy. He's one-half of this year's official song for the World Cup, "Dai Dai," led by Shakira. The song is a mesh of their musical landscapes, Afrobeats and Latin rhythms, an undeniably global, multilingual pop track. In one verse, they name a number of the world's most famous soccer players and countries competing in this year's World Cup. While the Super Bowl is famed for its halftime show, such performances are not commonplace in soccer, with events like the Champions League final featuring a pre-match concert. This year's World Cup halftime performance will also feature some characters from "Sesame Street," as well as Muppets like Kermit and Miss Piggy.

cards.headline: Karolina Muchova defeats Coco Gauff at Wimbledon in dramatic tiebreaker semifinal
cards.teaser: Karolina Muchova ended Coco Gauff's run at Wimbledon with a 6-2, 1-6, 7-6 (10) victory Thursday that ended with a drama-filled tiebreaker.
cards.body:
Karolina Muchova ended Coco Gauff's run at Wimbledon with a 6-2, 1-6, 7-6 (10) victory Thursday that ended with a drama-filled tiebreaker, to become the fourth Czech woman in the last six years to reach the final of the grass-court Grand Slam. It will be the ninth-ranked Muchova's second Grand Slam final after losing to Iga Swiatek in the 2023 French Open championship match.

Muchova could face another Czech player in Saturday's final, with Linda Noskova to play Marta Kostyuk of Ukraine in the other semifinal. For Gauff, it was still her most successful Wimbledon. Previously, the seventh-ranked American had gone only as far as the fourth round three times, including during her breakthrough run as a 15-year-old in 2019.

The men's semifinals on Friday feature top-ranked and defending champion Jannik Sinner against seven-time Wimbledon winner Novak Djokovic and French Open champion Alexander Zverev against British wild card Arthur Fery.

cards.headline: Park Vista Community High School football team targets state playoffs after strong 2025 finish
cards.body:
Park Vista Community High School's football team is building on late-season momentum as the Cobras set their sights on the state playoffs in 2026. The Cobras struggled to find their footing early in 2025, but finished strong, winning four of their last five games. Senior Harris Bender said the team felt good throughout the second half of that season. The team is working towards being able to carry that through the whole season, and all the pieces are in place now. It is just about executing. The ultimate goal is the state playoffs and eventually a state title, something the program has not achieved since 2017.

Park Vista head football coach Donald Hanna said the team has to take it one game at a time and cannot look past anyone. The Cobras have to handle business weekly, and if they do that and do their job, that will get them in the playoffs. Senior Erik Lee said coming in, he feels like the team has the guys needed to get it done, but the Cobras also have to put the work in to get there as well. Senior Justice Jones said it is going to feel amazing because he already knows it is going to happen. Park Vista opens the 2026 season on the road against Atlantic in August.

hero.headline: 18th Annual Treasure Coast Seafood Festival Returns to Vero Beach in November
hero.body:
The 18th Annual Treasure Coast Seafood Festival is returning to Vero Beach this November. Under The Sun Promotions, Inc. is organizing the event.

The festival has become an annual gathering in Vero Beach, drawing seafood enthusiasts to the Treasure Coast for fresh seafood and community entertainment. This year marks the 18th consecutive year for the event.

Under The Sun Promotions, Inc. is handling the festival planning and coordination. The company has organized the event in previous years.

The festival is scheduled for November 2026 in Vero Beach. Specific dates and venue details for this year's event were announced this week by the organizers.

Florida's annual back-to-school sales tax holiday runs from July 20 through Aug. 20, 2026, providing 32 days of tax-free shopping on qualifying purchases. The holiday covers clothing, bags and accessories under $100 per item, school supplies under $50 per item, learning aids and puzzles under $30 per item, and computers and accessories under $1,500 per item. Qualifying clothing includes shirts, pants, dresses, shoes, uniforms and athletic wear, while bags include backpacks, handbags, diaper bags and fanny packs. Excluded items include briefcases, suitcases, watches, jewelry, skis, swim fins and roller blades. Tax-free school supplies include pens, pencils, notebooks, binders, scissors, glue, lunch boxes, flashcards, jigsaw puzzles and educational toys. Qualifying computers include laptops, desktops, tablets, electronic book readers and calculators, along with accessories such as keyboards, mice, monitors without TV tuners, printers, modems, routers and educational software.

Items ordered online during the holiday period qualify for the exemption even if delivered after Aug. 20. Items purchased with rain checks issued during the holiday remain tax-free, and using gift cards to buy eligible items qualifies regardless of when the gift card was purchased. The tax exemption is not available at theme parks, entertainment complexes, hotels, public lodging establishments or airports. Florida retailers have no option to opt out of the sales tax holiday, and all qualifying purchases must be processed tax-free during the designated period.

cards.headline: Florida Department of Law Enforcement conducts 24 immigration arrests in Martin County
cards.teaser: FDLE conducted two dozen immigration arrests in Martin County on Tuesday as part of broader enforcement activity across South Florida.
cards.body:
According to data kept by the Florida Department of Law Enforcement, 24 immigration arrests were conducted in Martin County on Tuesday. The Martin County Sheriff's Office confirms FDLE was the agency behind the arrests.

According to NBC News, ICE arrested 10,000 people over five days this month. Renata Castro, an immigration attorney based in Coral Springs, said she has seen more detained cases across her desk and is seeing a lot more traffic-related detention resulting in immigration detention. Castro said the approach under former Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem was markedly different, with a lot of arrests without a warrant and a big spectacle overall. Immigration attorneys previously questioned the legality of many detentions carried out during Noem's tenure. Markwayne Mullin replaced Noem as Homeland Security Secretary in March.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie soccer stadium groundbreaking set for November with 2028 opening
hero.teaser: Port St. Lucie SC released new renderings of its 6,000-seat stadium at the Walton & One development, with groundbreaking anticipated in November.
hero.body:
Professional soccer is still set to begin next year in Port St. Lucie, and the club this week released new renderings of its 6,000-seat stadium. The stadium will be built at the Walton & One development, a 46-acre mixed-use redevelopment project located along U.S. 1 and Walton Road. Representatives for Port St. Lucie SC announced Friday that groundbreaking is anticipated later this year, with current plans targeting November.

While the club's inaugural season begins in 2027, the future stadium is scheduled to open in early 2028. The team has not announced where they plan to play next year while the facility is under construction. The club posted Thursday on social media that their home venue will be a place where soccer, community, and unforgettable moments will come together. The team also stated that every space has been designed to create unforgettable experiences, from matchdays to concerts, festivals, and community events, calling it a destination built for everyone.

Calling it a year-round gathering place, the club said the 6,000-seat venue will have the flexibility to grow in capacity. The team also said this week that ticket deposits are currently available online. It was announced last October that the city had been awarded a United Soccer League League One Team. St. Lucie city council members unanimously approved both the funding and operating agreements.

The city said the stadium is an $80 million economic investment, and no taxpayer money will be used for its construction. Diego Delledonne, the club's chief operating officer, released a statement Friday, though the specific content of that statement was not provided. The stadium project represents a significant development for the city as it prepares to welcome professional soccer to the community for the first time.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie teen surprised with FIFA World Cup finals flag bearer honor
cards.teaser: Enrique Rosario Liz, a Port St.
cards.body:
Enrique Rosario Liz, a Port St. Lucie teenager named Youth of the Year for the Southeast Region of the Boys & Girls Clubs of America, was surprised Friday at the Boys & Girls Club of St. Lucie County in Fort Pierce with news that he will serve as one of 12 club members from across the country selected to be an official Coca-Cola flag bearer at the FIFA World Cup finals on July 19. The surprise came courtesy of the Boys & Girls Clubs of America and their partnership with the Coca-Cola Company. Rosario Liz had already been juggling a packed summer, preparing for move-in at the University of Florida and an internship, but said the World Cup had been on his mind, forcing his parents to watch every game. When the box containing the news was walked into the room surrounded by fellow club members, Rosario Liz said the announcement was crazy and insane. Along with the trip, he received official gear inside the box.

Rosario Liz credited the Boys & Girls Club with shaping who he has become as a leader, saying the club helped him find what his leadership style was going to be and redefined what his definition of leadership was. He said it has been amazing to see how his community sees him as a leader and that he feels fortunate for everything that has come his way, calling the opportunities crazy and saying he is so lucky. He closed with a message for younger members of the club looking up to him, telling them to stay with their Boys & Girls Clubs because one day he wants to see each and every one of them in the same position that he is in right now.

hero.headline: Treasure Coast Traffic Report: Major Ramp and Road Closures Planned July 12-17
hero.teaser:
Motorists should prepare for overnight interstate ramp closures, extended neighborhood road closures and lane restrictions across Martin, St. Lucie and Indian River counties.

Driv
hero.body:
Motorists should prepare for overnight interstate ramp closures, extended neighborhood road closures and lane restrictions across Martin, St. Lucie and Indian River counties.

Drivers across the Treasure Coast could encounter delays during the week of July 10-17 as construction and maintenance continue on several major roadways.

The Florida Department of Transportation's latest weekly traffic report identifies multiple lane restrictions across Martin, St. Lucie and Indian River counties. FDOT placed additional emphasis on full road, ramp and bridge closures expected to have the greatest effect on motorists.

## Major closures to know about

### I-95 exit to Bridge Road closing overnight in Martin County

The southbound Interstate 95 exit ramp to County Road 708, also known as Bridge Road, at Exit 96 will be closed from **8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Sunday, July 12, through Thursday, July 16.**

Drivers will be directed to exit at Kanner Highway, travel south on Pratt Whitney Road and then head east on Bridge Road.

The closure is needed for roadway construction. Weather-related contingency dates are scheduled for July 19-23.

### Port St. Lucie neighborhood roads could close for several days

Extended closures are planned along several side streets near the SW Port St. Lucie Boulevard widening project.

Closures may begin at **7 a.m. Monday, July 13, and continue until 5 p.m. Friday, July 17,** on portions of SW Jaslo Avenue, SW Jacoby Avenue, SW McCullough Avenue, SW McCall Road and SW McHord Avenue.

The roads will close intermittently for drainage and utility installation. FDOT said adjacent roads will not be closed at the same time, and access to homes and businesses will be maintained.

Detours will generally use SW Paar Drive, SW McCain Street, SW McIntyre Street, SW Kabane Street and other nearby roads, depending on the closure location.

### I-95 ramp to Orange Avenue closing in Fort Pierce

The northbound I-95 exit ramp to westbound State Road 68, or Orange Avenue, will be closed from **8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Sunday, July 12, through Thursday, July 16.**

Motorists will be detoured using the exit to eastbound Orange Avenue, northbound Jenkins Road and westbound Loop Road before returning to westbound Orange Avenue.

The work includes paving and lighting installation. Contingency dates are July 19-23.

## Martin County traffic impacts

Motorists should expect overnight lane closures on I-95 between Bridge Road and the Martin-St. Lucie county line. Up to two lanes may close in each direction during overnight hours for milling, resurfacing and signage work.

On U.S. 1 in Stuart, two lanes may close intermittently between Fischer Street and Decker Avenue from 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Sunday through Friday for sign installation.

A1A between Shore Village Terrace and the Jensen Beach Causeway may be reduced to one lane at times from Monday through Friday for drainage work and pavement widening. Flaggers will maintain two-way traffic through the work zone.

Martin Highway between Stuart West Boulevard and Citrus Boulevard may also have intermittent overnight lane closures Tuesday through Thursday.

FDOT is additionally warning drivers in advance about several upcoming I-95 ramp closures at Martin Highway and Kanner Highway later in July and early August.

## St. Lucie County traffic impacts

Port St. Lucie Boulevard between Seafury Lane and Lennard Road may have daytime lane closures Monday through Friday. Two lanes may close overnight from Sunday through Friday for drainage work, milling and repaving.

U.S. 1 between Jennings Road and Golden Oak Trail may also have lane restrictions during both daytime and overnight hours.

On SW Port St. Lucie Boulevard, one lane may close between Jordin Avenue and Alcantarra Boulevard from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. Monday through Friday as crews continue the widening project.

Up to two lanes may close overnight on I-95 between Glades Cut-Off Road and the area just south of Okeechobee Road for milling and repaving.

Midway Road between Florida's Turnpike and Selvitz Road may continue to have intermittent weekday lane closures through September as part of the roadway widening project.

## North Causeway marine restrictions

The new A1A North Causeway Bridge remains open to vehicle traffic, but significant restrictions are planned for boaters using the Intracoastal Waterway.

The existing drawbridge will not open to marine traffic from 7 a.m. Thursday, July 16, through 6 p.m. Saturday, July 18. Boats capable of passing beneath the bridge without an opening may continue through.

Additional single-leaf openings, partial channel obstructions and temporary full channel closures are scheduled through July 24 as crews remove portions of the former drawbridge.

FDOT said the marine work will not affect vehicle traffic on the new bridge.

## Indian River County traffic impacts

One lane may remain closed on the 17th Street bridges between Indian River Boulevard and Indian Bay Drive as bridge rehabilitation continues.

At the new I-95 interchange at Oslo Road, one or two interstate lanes may close overnight Sunday through Thursday for bridge work, milling and resurfacing.

On 90th Avenue between Sebastian Boulevard and 87th Street, one lane may close overnight Sunday through Friday for construction associated with the 85th Street widening project.

Drivers traveling near Sebastian Inlet should also expect intermittent lane or shoulder closures on A1A through Friday, July 17. Flaggers will direct motorists through the work zone.

Sections of the north and south parking lots at Sebastian Inlet State Park will remain closed during construction of the new bridge. The closures are expected to continue through spring 2032, although the park and portions of both parking lots remain open.

## Plan ahead

Construction schedules may change because of weather or other unforeseen conditions. Motorists should allow additional travel time, follow posted detours and use caution around workers and equipment.

Real-time interstate traffic conditions are available through Florida 511. Updated lane closure information is also available through FDOT District Four.
